extracted.intended_audience: Caldecott committee members, children's librarians, illustrators, publishers, and scholars of children's literature
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative criteria for awarding the Caldecott Medal, including eligibility, definitions of a picture book and 'distinguished', and the specific pictorial qualities committee members must consider when selecting winners and honor books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal award definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal shall be awarded annually to the artist of the most distinguished American picture book for children published by an American publisher in the United States in English during the preceding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes that illustrations must be original work; honor books may be named; these shall be books that are also truly distinguished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist citizenship/residency restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is restricted to artists who are citizens or residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books published in a U.S. territory or U.S. commonwealth are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor book designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor books may be named; these shall be books that are also truly distinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honor books are treated as distinguished but distinct from the single Medal winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a picture book (visual experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'picture book for children' as distinguished from other books with illustrations, is one that essentially provides the child with a visual experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A picture book has a collective unity of story-line, theme, or concept, developed through the series of pictures of which the book is comprised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience — children up to age 14
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'picture book for children' is one for which children are an intended potential audience. The book displays respect for children’s understandings, abilities, and appreciations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children are defined as persons of ages up to and including fourteen and picture books for this entire age range are to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'distinguished'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Distinguished' is defined as: Marked by eminence and distinction; noted for significant achievement. Marked by excellence in quality. Marked by conspicuous excellence or eminence. Individually distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these senses of distinction when judging the work's merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist identity and posthumous awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist is the illustrator or co-illustrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The artist may be awarded the medal posthumously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original work requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Original work" means that the illustrations were created by this artist and no one else. Further, "original work" means that the illustrations are presented here for the first time and have not been previously published elsewhere in this or any other form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations reprinted or compiled from other sources are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: American publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "American picture book in the United States" means that books first published in previous years in other countries are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books published simultaneously in the U.S. and another country may be eligible. Books published in a U.S. territory or U.S. commonwealth are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement — In English
rubrics_metrics.description: "In English" means that the committee considers only books written and published in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement DOES NOT limit the use of words or phrases in another language where appropriate in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication year eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Published…in the preceding year" means that the book has a publication date in that year, was available for purchase in that year, and has a copyright date no later than that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book might have a copyright date prior to the year under consideration but, for various reasons, was not published until the year under consideration. If a book is published prior to its year of copyright as stated in the book, it shall be considered in its year of copyright as stated in the book. The intent is that every book be eligible for consideration, but that no book be considered in more than one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Resident" specifies that author has established and maintains a residence in the United States, U.S. territory, or U.S. commonwealth as distinct from being a casual or occasional visitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee scope limited to eligible books
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee in its deliberations is to consider only books eligible for the award, as specified in the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee is not to consider the entire body of the work by an artist or whether the artist has previously won the award. The committee’s decision is to be made following deliberation about books of the specified calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of execution (artistic technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellence of execution in the artistic technique employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the technical mastery and execution of the illustrative medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial interpretation of story/theme/concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellence of pictorial interpretation of story, theme, or concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how well the pictures interpret and communicate the narrative, theme, or concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of illustration style
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of style of illustration to the story, theme or concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the stylistic choices support and suit the book’s story, theme, or concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delineation through pictures
rubrics_metrics.description: Delineation of plot, theme, characters, setting, mood or information through the pictures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how effectively the illustrations convey essential narrative and informational elements without relying solely on text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of presentation for a child audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellence of presentation in recognition of a child audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider presentation choices (layout, pacing, readability, visual appeal) with children’s perceptions and needs in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic-form limitation and self-contained entity
rubrics_metrics.description: The only limitation to graphic form is that the form must be one which may be used in a picture book. The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media (i.e., sound, film or computer program) for its enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative/graphic forms tied to external media that are required for enjoyment render a book ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of other book components when detrimental
rubrics_metrics.description: Each book is to be considered as a picture book. The committee is to make its decision primarily on the illustration, but other components of a book are to be considered especially when they make a book less effective as a children’s picture book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such other components might include the written text, the overall design of the book, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not an award for didactic intent or popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is not for didactic intent or for popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind the award is for distinguished illustrations and excellence of pictorial presentation for children, not instructional purpose or sales/popularity metrics.
